_source.what: The real Moon for the year 2000, to test boundary-sky's own Moon (a fixed Keplerian ellipse, data/bodies.json + orbit.js) against.
_source.reference: JPL Horizons API, target 301 (Moon), center 500@399 (geocenter), VECTORS, ecliptic of J2000.0, ICRF, no light-time correction, TT, every 6 h from 2000-01-01 12:00 TT (day 0 = JD 2451545.0) to 2000-12-31 12:00. Horizons reports its source as DE441.
_source.cross_check: Independent second source: astropy 8.0.3, builtin ephemeris (ERFA moon98, Meeus' 1998 lunar series), transformed to GeocentricMeanEcliptic J2000, at all 1461 times. Agreement with this table: median 2.5", worst 10.9" in angle, worst 47.4 km in distance. Control: the same comparison with the times shifted by 6 h disagrees by a median 3.27 deg in longitude, so the agreement is not built in.
_source.start_condition: The app's Moon has no calendar date (mean anomaly 0 at sim day 0). The experiment sets its mean anomaly at day 0 (M0) so its ecliptic longitude matches this table's at 2000-01-01 12:00 TT, the epoch its J2000 mean elements are valid for. Nothing else is fitted.
